dedupe_keys.name: usgs national minerals information center materials flow studies

description: This USGS collection brings together reports on materials flow, the movement of mineral materials through a supply chain from extraction to processing to finished product, organised by commodity. It covers dozens of commodities, among them arsenic, beryllium, cadmium, cobalt, copper, gallium, indium, lead, lithium, manganese, mercury, nickel, platinum-group metals, rare earths, silver, tantalum and tin, with titles such as recycling in the United States in a given year, flows from rechargeable batteries, tantalum supply chain mapping and conflict mineral supply chains. It is produced by the U.S. Geological Survey's National Minerals Information Center. Coverage is mostly the United States, with some global studies such as world copper smelting and platinum-group metal supply, and dates run from recycling studies for 1998 to a cobalt study to 2020. The reports are available online free as USGS publications. Caveats: many studies describe a single year two decades ago and are not updated, and methods differ between commodities. For simulation they provide stocks, flows, recycling rates and supply chain stages for material flow and network models of mineral supply, showing where a mine, smelter or trade disruption would propagate to manufacturing. It is related to the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries record in this catalogue, which gives the annual statistics.
